Incorporating SLOOS alongside the FOMC statement and Financial Stability Report tilts the tone to “moderately positive but guarded.” SLOOS around this period points to easier standards and terms for C&I loans to large and middle‑market firms and firmer demand—supportive of the statement’s strong business investment. Offsetting that, banks continued to tighten for CRE and certain consumer credit (e.g., credit cards/auto), with softer demand for some residential mortgages—consistent with the noted moderation in household spending. Combined with the FSR’s elevated valuation pressures and rising nonfinancial business leverage, the credit survey evidence argues for a slightly more cautious read than a macro‑only take.
